name: Zhiva
description: Goddess of life, living nature, and vital force. The divine counterpart to Marzanna whose reign begins when winter dies.
mythology: Zhiva (the Alive One) is the goddess of life, living nature, and vital force. She is the divine embodiment of vitality — the force that animates all living things. She is the counterpart and rival to Marzanna: when Marzanna's effigy is burned or drowned in the spring ritual, Zhiva's reign begins. She is worshipped as Siwa by the Polabian Slavs at Ratibor. She appears as a beautiful young woman in summer garments, bringing flowers and abundance wherever she steps. The cuckoo is sacred to her — its call predicts how many more years you will live. She represents the immortal, ever-renewing life force of nature itself.
